17 Nov Come for the Riesling, Stay for the Cab Franc: New York Is Leaning Cab Franc Forward

Posted at 09:55h in *, Wine by Allison Levine
0 Likes
Share

“Come for the Riesling, stay for the Cabernet Franc.”

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:02
Instaread

This is a common phrase heard in New York’s Finger Lakes wine region. And it might challenge the common idea that the Finger Lakes is all about white wine. Riesling may have helped put the Finger Lakes on the wine map, but Cabernet Franc is making a name for itself. And not just in the Finger Lakes but across New York State. From the Finger Lakes to the Hudson Valley to Long Island, producers are embracing Cabernet Franc as a grape that can thrive in their growing conditions.

Today, Cabernet Franc is New York’s most widely planted red Vitis vinifera grape, with 638 acres planted across the state. Through Cab Franc Forward, a winery-founded and led initiative, producers are working together to champion Cabernet Franc as New York’s defining red grape.

I recently wrote about New York Cabernet Franc on Please The Palate Substack.
